notes: The year-character series is verifiable today against two independent published anchors that no source disputes. The Phugpa month/day calculation has a validated exact-rational implementation but its own publication contract requires almanac conformance before dates are presented, so those examples stay inventory_only and name the specific gate.

examples.location: 1027 CE, the year the first rabjung begins
examples.description: The canonical anchor of the Tibetan sexagenary era. Every published rabjung table starts here, so an implementation that misses it is wrong at the origin.

author_judgment.quotation: The first rabjung begins in the female Fire-Rabbit year, 1027 CE.

examples.description: Tibetan and Chinese share one sexagenary cycle, differing only in naming. Checking the Tibetan series against a Chinese anchor 957 years from the rabjung origin proves the series is not merely fitted to its own starting point. This example exists because an earlier implementation used a private element anchor and returned Wood Mouse for 1996 instead of Fire Mouse - it passed a 1027 check and failed here.

claims.author_states: 1984 CE is Jia-Zi: a Wood year.
1984 CE is Jia-Zi: a Mouse (Rat) year.
1996 CE is Bing-Zi: a Fire Mouse year, not Wood.

examples.location: Structural properties of a 60-year cycle over 5 elements and 12 animals
examples.description: Each element must govern exactly two consecutive years, and each element/animal pair must recur exactly once per sixty years. An off-by-one in the element pairing satisfies neither.

claims.author_states: Sixty consecutive years yield sixty distinct element/animal/polarity characters.
Each element governs exactly twelve years per sixty-year cycle, in consecutive male/female pairs.
Polarity alternates strictly year by year.
